PSA.38.13-14.text: The psalmist stays silent like a deaf and mute man

PSA.38.15-16.text: The psalmist waits for the LORD to answer him

PSA.38.17-18.text: The psalmist confesses his sin and his pain

PSA.38.19-20.text: Many enemies hate the psalmist without reason

PSA.38.21-22.text: The psalmist asks the LORD to come quickly and help

PSA.39.1-1.text: The psalmist decides to guard his tongue

PSA.39.2-3.text: The psalmist cannot stay silent and begins to speak

PSA.39.4-5.text: The psalmist asks the LORD how short his life is

PSA.39.6-7.text: The psalmist says life is empty; his hope is in the Lord

PSA.39.8-9.text: The psalmist asks the Lord to free him from his sins

PSA.39.10-11.text: The psalmist asks the Lord to stop his punishment

PSA.39.12-13.text: The psalmist asks God to hear him before he dies

PSA.40.1-2.text: God heard the psalmist and lifted him out of a pit

PSA.40.3-4.text: God gave the psalmist a new song of praise

PSA.40.5-6.text: The psalmist says God’s wonders are too many to count

PSA.40.7-9.text: The psalmist says he delights to do God’s will

PSA.40.10-11.text: The psalmist declares God’s faithfulness, asks for mercy

PSA.40.12-13.text: The psalmist asks God to hurry and help him in trouble

PSA.40.14-15.text: The psalmist asks God to shame those who want to harm him

PSA.40.16-17.text: The psalmist asks God to help him, a poor and needy man

PSA.41.1-3.text: God blesses and protects the one who cares for the poor

PSA.41.4-6.text: The psalmist asks God to heal him; enemies wish him dead

PSA.41.7-9.text: Enemies and a close friend turn against the psalmist

PSA.41.10-12.text: The psalmist asks God to raise him up and keep him

PSA.41.13-13.text: The psalmist blesses the LORD, the God of Israel

PSA.42.1-2.text: The psalmist longs for God like a deer for water

PSA.42.3-4.text: The psalmist weeps and remembers worshiping at God’s house

PSA.42.5-6.text: The psalmist tells his soul to hope in God

PSA.42.7-8.text: The psalmist feels overwhelmed, but God’s love is with him

PSA.42.9-10.text: The psalmist asks God why he is forgotten and mocked

PSA.42.11-11.text: The psalmist again tells his soul to hope in God

PSA.43.1-2.text: The psalmist asks God to defend him against unjust men

PSA.43.3-4.text: The psalmist asks God’s light and truth to lead him

PSA.43.5-5.text: The psalmist tells himself to hope in God and praise him

PSA.44.1-2.text: The people remember how God drove out the nations

PSA.44.3-4.text: The people say God, not swords, won the land

PSA.44.5-6.text: The people trust God, not weapons, to defeat enemies

PSA.44.7-8.text: The people praise God, who saves from enemies

PSA.44.9-11.text: The people say God has let enemies defeat Israel

PSA.44.12-14.text: The people say God has made Israel a joke to nations

PSA.44.15-17.text: The people feel shame, though faithful to God

PSA.44.18-22.text: The people stayed true to God but face death

PSA.44.23-24.text: The people ask God to wake up and not reject Israel

PSA.44.25-26.text: The people ask God to rise up and redeem Israel

PSA.45.1-2.text: The psalmist speaks verses of praise to the king

PSA.45.3-4.text: The psalmist tells the king to ride out for justice

PSA.45.5-7.text: God anointed the king who loves what is right

PSA.45.8-9.text: The king enjoys fine perfumes, music and royal women

PSA.45.10-11.text: The bride is told to forget her family and bow to the king

PSA.45.12-13.text: Rich people honor the glorious princess with gifts

PSA.45.14-15.text: The princess and her friends joyfully enter the palace

PSA.45.16-17.text: The king’s sons will rule and nations will praise him

PSA.46.1-3.text: God is a safe place, so believers do not fear disasters

PSA.46.4-5.text: God is with his city and will help it

PSA.46.6-7.text: The LORD protects his people while nations rage

PSA.46.8-9.text: The LORD ends wars and destroys weapons across the earth

PSA.46.10-11.text: God tells people to be still and know he is God

PSA.47.1-2.text: All peoples should clap and shout to God, the great King

PSA.47.3-5.text: God defeats nations for his people and goes up with joy

PSA.47.6-7.text: People are told to sing praises to God the King

PSA.47.8-9.text: God reigns over the nations on his holy throne

PSA.48.1-3.text: The LORD is great and is praised in Zion, his holy city

PSA.48.4-6.text: Kings advance together but flee in terror

PSA.48.7-8.text: God destroys ships and will keep his city forever

PSA.48.9-10.text: The people think about God’s love in the temple

PSA.48.11-11.text: Zion and Judah rejoice because of God’s judgments

PSA.48.12-13.text: People should tour Zion and tell the next generation

PSA.48.14-14.text: God will guide his people forever, even until death

PSA.49.1-2.text: The psalmist calls all people, rich and poor, to listen

PSA.49.3-5.text: The psalmist will speak wisdom and does not fear trouble

PSA.49.6-8.text: No one can pay God to save another person’s life

PSA.49.9-10.text: Wise and foolish people all die and leave wealth to others

PSA.49.11-11.text: Graves are the lasting homes of people who owned land

PSA.49.12-13.text: Even wealthy people die like animals

PSA.49.14-15.text: Death rules the proud, but God will save the psalmist

PSA.49.16-17.text: A rich man takes nothing with him when he dies

PSA.49.18-20.text: A rich man without understanding dies like the animals

PSA.50.1-2.text: God speaks and calls the whole earth from Zion

PSA.50.3-5.text: God comes to judge his people and gathers the faithful

PSA.50.6-6.text: The heavens declare that God is Judge

PSA.50.7-8.text: God speaks to Israel and testifies against the people

PSA.50.9-11.text: God does not need animal sacrifices; all animals are his

PSA.50.12-13.text: God is not hungry and does not eat meat or drink blood

PSA.50.14-15.text: God tells people to give thanks and call on him

PSA.50.16-17.text: God rebukes the wicked who hate his instruction

PSA.50.18-20.text: The wicked befriend thieves and speak evil and lies

PSA.50.21-22.text: God rebukes those who forget him and warns of judgment

PSA.50.23-23.text: God honors those who give thanks and live rightly

PSA.51.1-2.text: The writer asks God to show mercy and wash away sin

PSA.51.3-4.text: The writer knows his sin is against God alone

PSA.51.5-6.text: The writer is sinful from birth; God wants truth inside

PSA.51.7-9.text: The writer asks God to make him clean and forgive sins

PSA.51.10-11.text: The writer asks God for a clean heart and to stay near

PSA.51.12-13.text: The writer asks for joy again and promises to teach sinners

PSA.51.14-16.text: The writer asks to be saved from guilt and will praise God

PSA.51.17-19.text: God wants a broken spirit; the writer prays for Zion

PSA.52.1-2.text: The writer asks a mighty man why he boasts of evil

PSA.52.3-3.text: The man loves evil more than good and lies more than truth

PSA.52.4-5.text: God will bring the deceitful man down to ruin forever

PSA.52.6-7.text: The righteous will mock the man who trusted in wealth

PSA.52.8-9.text: The writer trusts God and will praise him forever

PSA.53.1-3.text: Fools say there is no God, and no one does good

PSA.53.4-5.text: God puts to shame those who attack his people

PSA.53.6-6.text: The writer longs for God to save Israel from Zion

PSA.54.1-3.text: The writer asks God to save him from ruthless men

PSA.54.4-5.text: God is the writer’s helper against his enemies

PSA.54.6-7.text: The writer will give thanks to God, who saved him

PSA.55.1-3.text: The writer cries to God about his enemies

PSA.55.4-5.text: The writer is full of fear and terror

PSA.55.6-7.text: The writer wishes he could fly away like a dove

PSA.55.8-9.text: The writer wants shelter and sees violence in the city

PSA.55.10-11.text: Evil and trouble fill the city day and night

PSA.55.12-14.text: The writer is hurt by a close friend, not an enemy

PSA.55.15-15.text: The writer asks God to let death take the wicked

PSA.55.16-18.text: The writer calls to God, and God saves him

PSA.55.19-19.text: God will hear and humble those who do not fear him

PSA.55.20-21.text: A false friend speaks smoothly but plans war

PSA.55.22-23.text: Believers can give their burdens to the LORD

PSA.56.1-2.text: The psalmist asks God for mercy against enemies

PSA.56.3-4.text: The psalmist trusts God and is not afraid

PSA.56.5-6.text: Enemies twist the psalmist’s words and plan to kill him

PSA.56.7-8.text: The psalmist asks God to judge and remember his tears

PSA.56.9-11.text: The psalmist knows God is on his side and trusts him

PSA.56.12-13.text: The psalmist will thank God for saving him from death

PSA.57.1-1.text: The psalmist asks God for mercy and takes refuge in him

PSA.57.2-3.text: The psalmist cries to God, who saves him from enemies

PSA.57.4-5.text: The psalmist is among cruel enemies and praises God

PSA.57.6-6.text: The psalmist’s enemies dig a pit and fall into it

PSA.57.7-8.text: The psalmist’s heart is steady and he will sing to God

PSA.57.9-11.text: The psalmist will praise God among the nations

PSA.58.1-2.text: The psalmist asks if rulers really judge fairly

PSA.58.3-5.text: The wicked are false from birth and refuse to listen

PSA.58.6-8.text: The psalmist asks God to stop the wicked

PSA.58.9-11.text: The righteous will see that God judges the earth

PSA.59.1-2.text: The psalmist asks God to save him from violent men

PSA.59.3-4.text: Fierce men plot against the psalmist, who is innocent

PSA.59.5-5.text: The psalmist asks God to punish the wicked nations

PSA.59.6-7.text: Enemies prowl the city like dogs and speak cruel words

PSA.59.8-9.text: God laughs at the nations; the psalmist waits for God

PSA.59.10-11.text: The psalmist asks God to scatter his enemies

PSA.59.12-13.text: The psalmist asks God to end the pride of his enemies

PSA.59.14-15.text: Enemies prowl like dogs and growl when not satisfied

PSA.59.16-17.text: The psalmist will sing of God’s strength and love

PSA.60.1-1.text: The psalmist asks God to restore his rejected people

PSA.60.2-3.text: The psalmist asks God to heal the shaken land

PSA.60.4-5.text: The psalmist asks God to save the people he loves

PSA.60.6-7.text: God speaks from his sanctuary and claims the land

PSA.60.8-9.text: God claims Moab, Edom and Philistia

PSA.60.10-12.text: The psalmist asks God for help against the enemy

PSA.61.1-3.text: The psalmist calls to God to lead him to safety

PSA.61.4-5.text: The psalmist asks to live safely with God

PSA.61.6-7.text: The psalmist asks God to give the king a long life

PSA.61.8-8.text: The psalmist promises to praise God and keep his vows

PSA.62.1-2.text: The psalmist finds rest and safety in God alone

PSA.62.3-4.text: The psalmist asks how long enemies will attack him

PSA.62.5-6.text: The psalmist tells himself to rest in God alone

PSA.62.7-8.text: The psalmist urges people to trust God at all times

PSA.62.9-10.text: The psalmist warns people not to trust in wealth

PSA.62.11-12.text: The psalmist says God is strong and will repay everyone

PSA.63.1-2.text: The psalmist longs for God in a dry land

PSA.63.3-4.text: The psalmist will praise God for his loving devotion

PSA.63.5-6.text: The psalmist is satisfied and thinks of God at night

PSA.63.7-8.text: The psalmist sings of God’s help and holds on to God

PSA.63.9-10.text: The psalmist says his enemies will be destroyed

PSA.63.11-11.text: The king will rejoice in God and liars will be silent

PSA.64.1-2.text: The psalmist asks God to protect him from the wicked

PSA.64.3-4.text: Wicked people use cruel words like swords and arrows

PSA.64.5-6.text: Wicked people plan evil in secret and think none sees

PSA.64.7-9.text: God will strike the wicked and all people will fear God

PSA.64.10-10.text: The righteous will rejoice in the LORD and trust him

PSA.65.1-3.text: The psalmist praises God who hears prayer and forgives sins

PSA.65.4-4.text: Those whom God chooses are blessed to live near him

PSA.65.5-5.text: God answers with great deeds and is hope for all the earth

PSA.65.6-7.text: God made the mountains and calmed the seas and nations

PSA.65.8-9.text: God cares for the earth and gives it water

PSA.65.10-12.text: God waters the land and the harvest is plentiful

PSA.65.13-13.text: Pastures and valleys shout and sing for joy

PSA.66.1-2.text: The psalmist calls all the earth to praise God

PSA.66.3-4.text: All the earth bows down and sings praise to God

PSA.66.5-7.text: The psalmist asks people to see what God has done

PSA.66.8-9.text: Peoples should bless God for keeping us alive

PSA.66.10-12.text: God tested his people through hardship, then gave plenty

PSA.66.13-15.text: The psalmist will bring offerings and keep his vows

PSA.66.16-18.text: The psalmist tells those who fear God what God has done

PSA.66.19-20.text: God has heard the psalmist’s prayer and is praised

PSA.67.1-2.text: The psalmist asks God to bless so nations know his ways

PSA.67.3-4.text: All peoples should praise God, who judges justly

PSA.67.5-6.text: Peoples should praise God for the harvest and blessing

PSA.67.7-7.text: God blesses his people and all the earth will fear him

PSA.68.1-3.text: God scatters his enemies, and the righteous rejoice

PSA.68.4-6.text: God cares for the fatherless, widows and the lonely

PSA.68.7-8.text: The earth shakes when God goes before his people

PSA.68.9-10.text: God sends rain and provides for his poor people

PSA.68.11-13.text: God gives the command, and women announce victory

PSA.68.14-16.text: God chose a mountain to live in forever

PSA.68.17-18.text: God’s chariots are many, and he went up on high

PSA.68.19-21.text: The psalmist praises God who saves and crushes enemies

PSA.68.22-23.text: God promises to bring his people back and defeat foes

PSA.68.24-25.text: People see God’s procession into the sanctuary

PSA.68.26-27.text: Israel’s tribes are called to bless God together

PSA.68.28-29.text: Kings will bring gifts as God shows his strength

PSA.68.30-31.text: The psalmist asks God to scatter nations that love war

PSA.68.32-33.text: All kingdoms of the earth should sing to God

PSA.68.34-35.text: The psalmist says God gives strength to his people

PSA.69.1-2.text: The psalmist asks God to save him from deep waters

PSA.69.3-4.text: The psalmist is tired from crying and has many enemies

PSA.69.5-6.text: The psalmist asks that others not be shamed through him

PSA.69.7-9.text: The psalmist bears shame out of zeal for God’s house

PSA.69.10-12.text: People mock the psalmist when he weeps and fasts

PSA.69.13-15.text: The psalmist asks God to rescue him from sinking

PSA.69.16-17.text: The psalmist asks God to answer him quickly

PSA.69.18-19.text: The psalmist asks God to redeem him from his foes

PSA.69.20-21.text: No one comforts the psalmist; people give him vinegar

PSA.69.22-23.text: The psalmist asks God to bring trouble on his enemies

PSA.69.24-25.text: The psalmist asks God to pour out anger on enemies

PSA.69.26-27.text: The psalmist says his enemies persecute those God struck

PSA.69.28-29.text: The psalmist asks God to remove enemies and protect him

PSA.69.30-31.text: The psalmist will praise God with song and thanks

PSA.69.32-33.text: The humble will rejoice because God hears the needy

PSA.69.34-36.text: All creation should praise God, who will save Zion

PSA.70.1-3.text: The psalmist asks God to hurry and save him

PSA.70.4-5.text: The psalmist is poor and asks God to come quickly

PSA.71.1-3.text: The psalmist asks God to rescue and save him

PSA.71.4-5.text: The psalmist asks God to save him from wicked people

PSA.71.6-7.text: The psalmist has trusted God since he was born

PSA.71.8-9.text: The psalmist asks God not to leave him when he is old

PSA.71.10-11.text: The psalmist’s enemies say God has left him

PSA.71.12-13.text: The psalmist asks God to hurry and shame his accusers

PSA.71.14-16.text: The psalmist promises to praise God all day long

PSA.71.17-18.text: The psalmist will tell the next generation of God’s power

PSA.71.19-20.text: God is great and will restore the psalmist after troubles

PSA.71.21-22.text: The psalmist will praise God with the harp and lyre

PSA.71.23-24.text: The psalmist will shout for joy and praise God

PSA.72.1-3.text: The psalmist asks God to give the king justice

PSA.72.6-7.text: The king’s rule is like rain, and the righteous flourish

PSA.72.8-10.text: The king will rule widely and other kings bring gifts

PSA.72.11-12.text: All kings will serve the king, who saves the needy

PSA.72.13-14.text: The king will pity and save the poor and oppressed

PSA.72.15-16.text: People will pray for the king and the land will prosper

PSA.72.17-17.text: The king’s name will last forever and bless all nations

PSA.72.18-20.text: The psalmist praises God, and David’s prayers end

PSA.73.1-3.text: The psalmist almost slipped when he envied the wicked

PSA.73.4-5.text: The wicked have easy lives and no troubles

PSA.73.6-7.text: The wicked are proud, violent, and full of evil thoughts

PSA.73.8-9.text: The wicked mock people and speak against heaven

PSA.73.10-12.text: The wicked say God does not know, and grow rich

PSA.73.13-15.text: The psalmist feels his pure life was for nothing

PSA.73.16-17.text: The psalmist enters God’s sanctuary and understands

PSA.73.18-20.text: God will destroy the wicked suddenly

PSA.73.21-22.text: The psalmist admits he was senseless before God

PSA.73.23-24.text: God holds the psalmist’s hand and guides him

PSA.73.25-26.text: The psalmist wants only God, his strength forever

PSA.73.27-28.text: The psalmist draws near to God, but the unfaithful perish

PSA.74.1-2.text: The psalmist asks why God has rejected his people

PSA.74.3-6.text: The psalmist asks God to look at the ruined sanctuary

PSA.74.7-8.text: Enemies burn God’s sanctuary and every meeting place

PSA.74.9-11.text: The psalmist asks how long the enemy will mock God

PSA.74.12-13.text: God is King and has shown his power over the sea

PSA.74.14-15.text: God crushed Leviathan and controlled the waters

PSA.74.16-17.text: God made day, night, sun, moon, summer and winter

PSA.74.18-19.text: The psalmist asks God to remember his afflicted people

PSA.74.20-21.text: The psalmist asks God to remember the covenant and the poor

PSA.74.22-23.text: The psalmist asks God to rise up and defend his cause

PSA.75.1-3.text: People thank God, who says he will judge fairly

PSA.75.4-6.text: God warns the proud and the wicked not to boast

PSA.75.7-8.text: God judges and makes the wicked drink from his cup

PSA.75.9-10.text: The psalmist will praise God, who lifts up the righteous

PSA.76.1-3.text: God is known in Israel and lives in Zion

PSA.76.4-5.text: God is full of light, and mighty men cannot fight

PSA.76.6-7.text: At God’s rebuke, horses and riders lie still

PSA.76.8-9.text: God judges from heaven and saves the lowly

PSA.76.10-10.text: Even human anger will bring praise to God

PSA.76.11-12.text: The psalmist urges people to keep vows to God

PSA.77.1-1.text: The psalmist cries aloud to God

PSA.77.2-3.text: In trouble, the psalmist seeks God but finds no comfort

PSA.77.4-5.text: The psalmist cannot sleep or speak and thinks of the past

PSA.77.6-7.text: The psalmist asks if God will reject his people forever

PSA.77.8-9.text: The psalmist asks if God’s love and promise have ended

PSA.77.10-10.text: The psalmist is grieved that God’s power has changed

PSA.77.11-12.text: The psalmist will remember and think about God’s deeds

PSA.77.13-15.text: God is holy and great, and he redeemed his people

PSA.77.16-17.text: The waters shake and storms show God’s power

PSA.77.18-20.text: God led his people through the sea by Moses and Aaron

PSA.78.1-2.text: The psalmist asks his people to listen to his teaching

PSA.78.3-4.text: Fathers pass on God’s praises to the next generation

PSA.78.5-6.text: God commanded fathers to teach his law to children

PSA.78.7-8.text: Children should trust God and not be like stubborn fathers

PSA.78.9-11.text: Ephraim’s archers turned back and broke God’s covenant

PSA.78.12-14.text: God did wonders in Egypt and led Israel through the sea

PSA.78.15-16.text: God gave Israel water from rocks in the wilderness

PSA.78.17-18.text: Israel kept sinning and tested God by demanding food

PSA.78.19-20.text: Israel doubted that God could give bread and meat

PSA.78.21-22.text: God was angry because Israel did not believe God

PSA.78.23-25.text: God gave Israel manna from heaven to eat

PSA.78.26-28.text: God sent birds as meat into Israel’s camp

PSA.78.29-30.text: God gave Israel the food that Israel craved

PSA.78.31-32.text: God killed Israel’s strongest men, but Israel kept sinning

PSA.78.33-34.text: When God killed many, Israel turned back to God

PSA.78.35-37.text: Israel remembered God but lied to him

PSA.78.38-38.text: God was merciful, forgave Israel, and held back his anger

PSA.78.39-41.text: Israel often grieved God in the wilderness

PSA.78.42-43.text: Israel forgot God’s power and his signs in Egypt

PSA.78.47-49.text: God sent hail and destroying angels against Egypt

PSA.78.50-51.text: God killed all the firstborn of Egypt

PSA.78.52-53.text: God led Israel safely like a flock

PSA.78.54-55.text: God brought Israel into the land and settled the tribes

PSA.78.56-57.text: Israel again tested God and turned away from him

PSA.78.58-59.text: Israel’s idols made God angry, so God rejected Israel

PSA.78.60-61.text: God abandoned Shiloh and let enemies take his strength

PSA.78.64-66.text: Priests died, then God rose up and defeated his enemies

PSA.78.67-69.text: God chose Judah and Mount Zion, not Ephraim

PSA.78.70-72.text: God chose David to be shepherd of Israel

PSA.79.1-3.text: Enemy nations destroyed Jerusalem and killed God’s people

PSA.79.4-5.text: Israel is mocked and asks how long God will be angry

PSA.79.6-7.text: The people ask God to punish nations that harmed Jacob

PSA.79.8-9.text: The people ask God to forgive sins and save Israel

PSA.79.10-11.text: The people ask God to answer the nations and free captives

PSA.79.12-13.text: The people ask God to repay neighbors and promise praise

PSA.80.1-3.text: The psalmist asks God to hear and to restore Israel

PSA.80.4-6.text: The psalmist asks how long God will be angry

PSA.80.7-8.text: The psalmist recalls how God planted a vine from Egypt

PSA.80.9-11.text: The vine grew and filled the whole land

PSA.80.12-13.text: The psalmist asks why God let the vine be ruined

PSA.80.14-16.text: The psalmist asks God to return and care for the vine

PSA.80.17-18.text: The psalmist asks God to help the man at God’s right hand

PSA.80.19-19.text: The psalmist asks God again to restore Israel

PSA.81.4-5.text: The feast is a rule God gave to Israel

PSA.81.6-7.text: God reminds Israel how he rescued the people

PSA.81.8-10.text: God tells Israel to listen and not worship other gods
